Test: biodiversity institutions

Source: R/test-docs.R
test_institution.Rd

Flags records within 100 m of a biodiversity institution (WGS84 geodesic distance, closed ball): herbaria, museums, botanic gardens, zoos and universities holding collections, where specimens are often georeferenced to the institution. The default gazetteer holds 18,245 points: the 6,080 institutions with coordinates in GBIF's Global Registry of Scientific Collections (GRSciColl), less five whose coordinates the zero test flags (they lie near (0, 0) or have a longitude of exactly 0, and are geocoding errors); 7,810 points from Wikidata (CC0), retrieved 2026-10-10: every botanical garden, natural history museum, zoo, aquarium and herbarium with coordinates, every museum whose subject is a natural-history field, and the museums of Wikipedia's lists of natural history museums (English, Arabic, Dutch, Esperanto, French, German and Portuguese editions) that have their own Wikidata coordinates; 700 further museums of those lists placed at the place the list gives for them, by its Wikidata coordinates or the GeoNames populated place of that name (source "Wikipedia", master_source says which); the three GeoNames places (CC BY 4.0) of CoordinateCleaner's table; and 3,652 gardens of Botanic Gardens Conservation International (BGCI) GardenSearch, retrieved 2026-10-10, used under the BGCI terms (https://www.bgci.org/terms-and-conditions/). The source column of reference_points() tells them apart.

Details

The column extension marks the 7,665 points from sources CoordinateCleaner's table does not draw on: Wikidata beyond the museums of the English list, and the lists of the other language editions. The other 10,580 points come from the registries CoordinateCleaner's table is compiled from (GRSciColl, which absorbed GRBio and mirrors Index Herbariorum, the English list, GeoNames and BGCI). Passing the points with extension FALSE as gazetteers = list(institution = ...) restricts the test to those sources (see the examples).

Fields

lon, lat.

Buffer

buffers = list(institution = 100), in metres.

CoordinateCleaner

Equivalent to cc_inst(). Its 40-gon buffer edge lies within 0.31 m of the 100 m circle. Its institutions table (9,773 points with coordinates) geocodes most of its 712 BGCI gardens and many of its Wikipedia museums itself, so its points can lie apart from the source coordinates used here. For 92 percent of the 345 Wikipedia museums it placed by hand a point of the default gazetteer lies within 5 km, for 52 percent within 100 m (91 and 46 percent for the points with extension FALSE). reference = "CoordinateCleaner" uses that table, and rbind() of reference_points() under both references, passed as gazetteers = list(institution = ...), flags records near either.

Custom gazetteer

gazetteers = list(institution = points), a data frame of longitude and latitude; see flag_occurrences().

See also

flag_occurrences(), flag_tests(), reference_info()

Other tests: test_age_equal, test_age_outlier, test_age_range_outlier, test_aohi, test_basis, test_capital, test_centroid, test_country_mismatch, test_dataset_ddmm, test_dataset_rounded, test_duplicate, test_equal, test_establishment, test_gbif_headquarters, test_gbif_issue, test_habitat, test_invalid, test_outlier, test_range, test_sea, test_spatiotemporal_outlier, test_urban, test_zero

Examples

x <- data.frame(decimalLongitude = c(16.3598, 15), decimalLatitude = c(48.2052, 47))
flag_occurrences(x, tests = "institution")$flag_institution
g <- reference_points("institution")
flag_occurrences(x, tests = "institution",
                 gazetteers = list(institution = g[!g$extension, ]))$flag_institution
